rv.q: David McVicar's new staging of Puccini's melodramatic thriller, unveiled on New Year's Eve, feels like a course correction—one that is less risky and more successful.
The result was a grand triumph that relegated the old Met Tosca to the list of forgotten flops.
No point of view can be just as bad as Bondy's unpleasant one and this cake seemed taken from the oven before it was done.

After a promising start, with a tingly attack on the opera's eerie opening fanfare, conductor Emmanuel Villaume fell apart bit by bit, fluffing innumerable details of Tosca's notoriously tricky in-and-out rhythms.
It was thrilling to see the other side of that passion as the tragedy wore on.

Back to the Future… This David McVicar production is nearly a decade in the making, with Luc Bondy’s combination of an erratic vision and Ikea furniture getting jeered and booed unexpectedly on its opening night performance.
